title: Predicting numbers
blurb: Not every answer is a category — sometimes AI predicts a number. Lay the line of best fit yourself.

steps.title: Two kinds of questions
steps.body:
So far your AIs answered **which kind?** — cat or dog, rose or daisy. That's **classification**.

But some questions don't have categories. *"How tall will this plant grow?"* *"What will this house sell for?"* The answer is a **number**. Predicting a number has its own name: **regression** — and the trick is to draw the best straight line through your examples.

steps.title: Lay the line yourself
steps.body: Below are data points. **Drag the two ring handles** to lay a straight line through them. The orange dashes are the **misses**, and the **error** number is how far off you are overall. Tune it until the error drops under the goal. (Stuck? **Snap to best fit** shows the perfect line.)

steps.title: That 'error' is how AI learns
steps.body:
Every orange dash was a **mistake** — the gap between a real dot and your line. Add them all up and you get the **error** (also called the **loss**). The best line is simply the one with the **smallest error** — that's exactly what you hunted for.

Pause on this, because it's huge: **learning = lowering the error.** A giant AI with billions of settings trains the same way you just did — guess, measure how wrong, adjust, repeat.

steps.title: The learning loop
steps.question: In one sentence, what does 'training' an AI really mean?
choices: Making the error as small as possible
steps.explain: Exactly — training means adjusting the model until the error is as small as it can be. You just did it by hand.

steps.title: The overfitting trap
steps.body:
You *could* draw a wild, wiggly line that hits **every** dot perfectly… but that's usually a trap. A line that bends to touch every dot has **memorized** the examples instead of learning the pattern — give it a new dot and it flails. That's **overfitting**.

Want to feel it? The **Regression Studio** lets you crank the curve from straight to super-bendy and watch it overfit on purpose.

steps.title: What you built 🎉
steps.body:
- **Classification** predicts a category; **regression** predicts a **number**
- You laid the **line of best fit** — the one with the smallest **error (loss)**
- **Training = lowering the error**, step by step — the heart of all AI
- A simple line that's 'close enough' usually beats a wiggly one that **overfits**

**Next up:** a different kind of AI you can actually *read* — the **decision tree**.
